lines: Imagine falling from the sky through a violent storm and waking up alone in a deadly jungle.
On 24 December 1971 a passenger plane is struck by lightning and breaks apart midair.
Seventeen year old Juliane Koepcke falls about 3000 meters while still strapped to her seat row.
She wakes up on the dark forest floor with a broken collarbone and a deep arm cut.
She also suffers from a painful eye injury and a severe concussion after the terrifying plunge.
Her biologist father previously taught her that following flowing water always leads back to people.
She finds a tiny creek and begins walking through the dense and dangerous Peruvian rainforest.
Days pass slowly as she follows the winding water toward a larger and safer river.
Up to 14 other passengers survive the initial crash but tragically die before any rescue arrives.
She spends 11 long days completely alone in the unforgiving jungle facing unimaginable odds.
After 9 days of difficult travel she finally discovers a remote lumberjack camp by the river.
She is found by local workers who provide medical help and bring her back to safety.
Juliane remains the only official survivor of LANSA Flight 508 against all odds and expectations.
Would you have the mental strength to survive 11 days alone in the dangerous rainforest?
draft_evening.title: The Girl Who Fell 3000 Meters And Survived

lines: If a fire alarm wakes you at night, do not stand up and run blindly through smoke.
Leo wakes up at 2 AM inside his home to a screeching smoke detector alarm above.
Thick black smoke fills his bedroom fast, leaving him under 60 seconds to make moves.
One. Get low and go right away because dangerous smoke always rises to the ceiling.
The cleanest air is near the floor, so Leo crouches low to breathe safely inside.
Two. Feel the door with the back of your hand before opening it to leave.
If the door is hot, do not open it, and use another way out fast.
Leo touches the wooden door with the back of his hand and feels cool surface.
Three. Close doors behind you as you move forward to slow down the fire spread.
Leo shuts the heavy bedroom door behind himself to block incoming heat and smoke.
He runs away out of the house into the cool night air to safety.
Official advice says get out, stay out, and call for help from outside always.
You must never go back inside a burning building for any reason at all.
Raging fire suddenly explodes through the roof, blasting heat across the entire front yard.
It was the perfect escape plan, but there was just one major problem remaining.
Leo needs to call for help, but his phone is still sitting inside.
part1.cliffhanger: Leo escaped the fire safely, but his phone is trapped inside and he must call for help without going back in.
